mil5.2.3:0.4: 3. Question on Fearing and Not Fearing Death
mil5.2.3:1.1: “Venerable Nāgasena, this too was said by the Blessed One:
mil5.2.3:1.2: ‘All tremble at the rod; all fear death.’ And he also said:
mil5.2.3:1.3: ‘The arahant has gone beyond all fear.’
mil5.2.3:1.4: Does the arahant, Venerable Nāgasena, tremble from fear of punishment? And do beings in hell, blazing, boiling, scorched and thoroughly burned, fear death as they pass away from that great hell with its flaming masses of fire?
mil5.2.3:1.5: If, Venerable Nāgasena, the Blessed One said
mil5.2.3:1.6: ‘All tremble at the rod; all fear death,’ then the statement ‘The arahant has gone beyond all fear’ is false.
mil5.2.3:1.8: ‘The arahant has gone beyond all fear,’ then the statement ‘All tremble at the rod; all fear death’ is also false.
mil5.2.3:1.9: This two-horned dilemma has now come to you, and it must be resolved by you.”
mil5.2.3:2.1: “Your majesty, the Blessed One did not speak those words with reference to arahants:
mil5.2.3:2.2: ‘All tremble at the rod; all fear death.’
mil5.2.3:2.3: The arahant is set apart from that case; for the arahant the cause of fear has been uprooted.
mil5.2.3:2.4: It was , your majesty, with reference to beings who still have defilements, who have an excessive view of self, and who are elated or dejected concerning pleasure and pain, that the Blessed One spoke those words:
mil5.2.3:2.5: ‘All tremble at the rod; all fear death.’
mil5.2.3:2.6: For the arahant, your majesty, every destination is cut off, every womb is destroyed, rebirth-linking is struck down, the supporting beams of the house are broken, every dwelling-place in existence is uprooted, all formations are cut off, wholesome and unwholesome kamma are destroyed, ignorance is shattered, consciousness has been made seedless, all defilements are burned, the worldly conditions are transcended. Therefore the arahant does not tremble at any fears.
mil5.2.3:3.1: Suppose, your majesty, a king had four chief ministers, protectors who had won his trust and favour, and he had placed them in positions of great authority.
mil5.2.3:3.2: Then, when some business arose, the king commanded everyone in his realm: ‘Let all of you pay me tribute; and you four chief ministers, carry out that business.’
mil5.2.3:3.3: Would those four chief ministers, your majesty, feel dread from fear of the tribute?”
mil5.2.3:3.6: “Because the king placed them in the highest position, venerable sir. They owe no tribute; they have gone beyond tribute. The king’s command, ‘Let all pay me tribute,’ was made with reference to the rest.”
mil5.2.3:3.7: “In the same way, your majesty, the Blessed One did not speak those words with reference to arahants. The arahant is set apart from that case; for the arahant the cause of fear has been uprooted. It was with reference to beings who still have defilements, who have an excessive view of self, and who are elated or dejected in pleasure and pain, that he said:
mil5.2.3:3.8: ‘All tremble at the rod; all fear death.’
mil5.2.3:3.9: Therefore the arahant does not tremble at any fears.”
mil5.2.3:4.1: “Venerable Nāgasena, that statement does not leave anything out; ‘all’ is a statement without exception.
mil5.2.3:4.2: Give me a further reason to establish it.”
mil5.2.3:5.1: “Suppose, your majesty, the headman of a village commanded his messenger: ‘Come, messenger, quickly gather before me all the villagers in the village.’
mil5.2.3:5.2: The messenger, saying ‘Yes, master,’ would stand in the middle of the village and call out three times: ‘All villagers in the village, assemble quickly before the master!’
mil5.2.3:5.3: Then the villagers, at the messenger’s word, would hurry and gather, and report to the headman: ‘All the villagers have assembled, master; do what you need to do.’
mil5.2.3:5.4: So, your majesty, in gathering the householder men, the headman commanded all the villagers, yet not all of those commanded assembled; only the householder men did. And the headman accepted this, thinking, ‘These are all my villagers.’ The many others who did not come (women and men, slaves and servants, hired hands and workers, sick villagers, cattle, buffalo, goats, sheep, and dogs) were all left uncounted, because the command ‘Let all assemble’ had been given with reference to the householder men alone.
mil5.2.3:5.5: In just the same way, your majesty, the Blessed One did not speak those words with reference to arahants. The arahant is set apart from that case; for the arahant the cause of fear has been uprooted. It was with reference to beings who still have defilements, who have an excessive view of self, and who are elated or dejected in pleasure and pain, that the Blessed One said:
mil5.2.3:5.6: ‘All tremble at the rod; all fear death.’
mil5.2.3:5.7: Therefore the arahant does not tremble at any fears.
mil5.2.3:6.1: There is, your majesty, a statement with exceptions whose meaning has exceptions; a statement with exceptions whose meaning has none; a statement without exceptions whose meaning has exceptions; and a statement without exceptions whose meaning has none.
mil5.2.3:6.2: The meaning must be accepted in each case accordingly.
mil5.2.3:7.1: The meaning, your majesty, should be established by five means: by the direct text (āhaccapada), by the essence (rasa), by the teacher’s lineage (ācariyavaṁsa), by one’s own understanding (adhippāya), and by the superiority of reasoning (kāraṇuttariyatā).
